headline: 📥 **THE OFFER ARRIVED AT 2:20 THIS AFTERNOON AND THE BUYER HAD ALREADY SIGNED IT.** Molly G. of Keller Williams Hoover emailed the full packet on 225 Willow Point — purchase agreement carrying the buyer’s signature, personal-property addendum, FHA addendum and a lender pre-approval — then texted ninety seconds later to be sure you saw it. ⭐ **SEVEN DAYS, FOUR TOURS, THREE BROKERAGES, AND NOT ONE AGENT EVER ARGUED THE PRICE.** That is the whole case for this board: the showings found the buyer, and the feedback said the number was never the problem. 🔴 **SHE ASKED IN WRITING TO BE TOLD IT WAS RECEIVED AND NOBODY HAS ANSWERED HER.** That is the one thing owed tonight, and it takes a minute. 🔍 And three buyer-side offices are still waiting on feedback from Sunday’s tour — two of them have now asked twice.

hotSignals.signal: 📥 **OFFER IN HAND — AND THE BUYER SIGNED BEFORE THE SELLER EVER SAW IT.** Molly G. of Keller Williams Hoover emailed the packet at 2:20:39 PM and texted ninety seconds later. Four documents together: the purchase agreement already buyer-signed, a personal-property addendum, an FHA addendum, and a lender pre-approval letter written to the full list price. ⭐ A buyer who signs first, on FHA, with financing already papered, is not shopping — that is a buyer trying to end the search. 🎯 **THE OFFERED PRICE IS NOT SHOWN HERE AND WAS NOT GUESSED** — it lives inside the PDF and nothing in this system can open an attachment. The pre-approval figure is the buyer’s ceiling, not their offer.
hotSignals.action: Open the PDF yourself and read the number before you speak to anyone. Then, tonight: reply to Molly acknowledging receipt — she asked in writing and has been waiting since 2:20 — and correct the flood-insurance figure you gave her at 2:51, which is roughly half what your own sellers’ escrow statement says. On an FHA file, flood is escrowed and underwritten; that number will surface either way. Call your sellers before you write anything to them.

hotSignals.signal: 🔥 **A THIRD AGENT CAME BACK ON HER OWN AT 5:51 THIS MORNING.** Angela W. of ARC Realty 280 — whose buyer toured Sunday and left in under ten minutes because the buyer arrived late, not because the house failed — wrote back unprompted calling it an adorable townhouse, and said her buyer is forwarding the listing to a husband who works out of town. ⭐ A buyer forwarding a house to the person who has to agree is the most common shape a second showing takes.
hotSignals.action: This stopped being a nice-to-have the moment the offer landed. A second live party is the only real leverage on the table. Call her, not email: does the husband want to see it, and when? Written outreach already went to her at 7:4x this morning — what is missing is your voice.

hotSignals.signal: ⏰ **THE OFFER WAS DECLARED THE NIGHT BEFORE AND ARRIVED A DAY LATE.** Molly G. texted at 6:17 PM Monday that her buyers wanted to write and she would have it over by morning; it landed at 2:20 the following afternoon. ⭐ Worth remembering rather than resenting — she also asked whether she was bidding against anyone, which is an agent protecting buyers she believes are serious.
hotSignals.action: Closed by events — the offer is in hand. Keep the pattern in mind: on this brokerage, a promised document runs about a half-day late.

hotSignals.signal: 🎉 **THE FIRST FEEDBACK THIS ADDRESS EVER PRODUCED, AND THE HEADLINE WAS WHAT SHE DIDN’T SAY.** Anna C. of A2 Properties toured and filed a form that never challenged the asking price. ⭐ Four tours across three brokerages in five days and not one agent argued the number — which is exactly the pattern a correctly priced listing produces.
hotSignals.action: The reply to her is still an unsent draft, second day running. Send it or delete it — but do not leave a colleague on read while you are negotiating an offer on the same house.

hotSignals.signal: 🎉 **SIGNATURE TO OPEN ESCROW IN ONE MORNING.** The contract-to-close details went to the title office at 11:34 AM and the closer answered in six minutes saying they would start the same day. The showings that produced this stopped mattering the moment the paper moved. ⭐ One scheduling detail worth catching now: your coordinator asked for this one as the SECOND closing, stacked back-to-back with another sale the same day.
hotSignals.action: Nothing to chase on the showing side — this one converted. The live item is the stacked closing date: it is movable in August and immovable in closing week. And the honest risk is unchanged — these buyers must close their own house first.

hotSignals.signal: 🎯 **A FIFTH SHOWING SATURDAY AT 3:00 PM from an agent who had never shown this house before** — and the read has still not come back. ⚠️ Separately, four independent agents have now filed the same verdict on this address, and the most recent added the worst staging score anywhere on this board.
hotSignals.action: Four days out, the odds of that form arriving are falling — this address returns feedback about half the time. Chase it by phone, not by form. And the lever that is not a price cut is still unpulled: a pre-inspection, because unknowns are exactly what a pre-inspection removes.

hotSignals.signal: 🔥 **THE ONLY UNQUALIFIED YES ON THIS BOARD, AND IT IS NOW DAY ELEVEN.** Amy G. of Ethos International filed it herself: interested YES, her buyers just started looking, they really like it, and it sits at the TOP of their list. She phoned from inside the house mid-showing. ⭐ She left priced-right blank — the objection is unasked, not absent.
hotSignals.action: A human call, today. Eleven days is well past the window where a machine outreach is appropriate, and she called you from inside the house, so a call back is returned rather than cold. Ask the price question she never answered — and get your seller to answer the basement lights she reported.

listings.status: 📥 OFFER RECEIVED — buyer-signed FHA packet, day 7

feedback.note: 🔥 UNPROMPTED AT 5:51 AM, REPLYING TO YOUR 7:15 PM ASK: “It is an adorable townhouse. Her husband works out of town and she will send the listing to him.” ⭐ THE TOUR RAN SHORT ONLY BECAUSE HER BUYER ARRIVED LATE — she said so herself at 7:09 PM — so nothing about the house failed; the read simply never got collected on site. 🎯 A buyer forwarding a listing to an out-of-town decision-maker is a second showing waiting to be booked. ✅ Agent outreach sent 7:5x AM.

🔥 “My buyers are interested in 225 Willow Point Cir. They actually really liked it” at 10:27 AM — then at 6:17 PM: “Buyers want to make an offer… I probably won't be able to get it to you until morning. Do you have any offers yet?” ⭐ SHE TOOK THE FIRST SHOWING THIS LISTING EVER HAD. Her only two reservations are a living-room ceiling mark and an unpatched closet, and she asked directly whether the sellers had corrected them. 🎯 She never raised the price. ⚠️ The sellers answered both in writing within the hour and that answer has still not reached her.

🎉 THE FIRST FEEDBACK THIS ADDRESS EVER PRODUCED, twenty minutes after you asked — by email, not through the showing system, which has never once issued a request here. ⭐ THE HEADLINE IS WHAT SHE DIDN'T SAY: asked directly how $185,000 read against everything her buyers have seen, she did not argue the number at all. 🔍 HER WORDS: the buyers “really liked it,” it “showed very well,” and “you can tell they definitely put in the work.” ⚠️ THREE CONCERNS, ALL COSMETIC BY HER OWN READ: a crack she thinks is a settled Sheetrock joint, whether crown molding is going back or being cut in with paint, and a patched laundry-room ceiling opening she assumes is a deliberate access panel.
